assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Target Branch section — either all set to 'main' (direct-to-main workflow) or bookend tasks set to 'main' with intermediate tasks set to the feature issue ID (feature-branch workflow)
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 tasks have '## Target Branch' set to 'main'. The impact-map.md confirms 'Selected mode: direct-to-main' and the summary-comment.md states 'direct-to-main — All tasks target main.' This is a consistent direct-to-main workflow.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:', not a placeholder, abbreviated value, or example string
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 digest files (task-1-digest.md through task-8-digest.md) exist, but they all contain placeholder values instead of actual SHA-256 hashes. For example, task-1-digest.md contains: '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:placeholder-digest-for-task-1-created-from-tc-9003'. The assertion requires exactly 64 lowercase hex characters after 'sha256-md:', but 'placeholder-digest-for-task-1-created-from-tc-9003' is not a 64-character hex string. All 8 digests fail this requirement.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: No task description contains any convention-aware enrichment section with 'Applies:' rationale in the prescribed format. Searching for 'Applies:' across all output files returned no results. There is no evidence of convention applicability validation having been performed per the shared/convention-applicability-rules.md specification.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: The impact-map.md states under '## Inherited Fields': 'Priority: Critical (inherited from TC-9003, will be propagated to all tasks)'. The task-creation-log.md confirms: 'priority: Critical inherited from TC-9003 (Feature priority is set and not "Undefined")' and shows each task receiving 'priority: Critical' in its additional_fields. The summary-comment.md also states: 'Priority: Critical (inherited from TC-9003, propagated to all tasks)'. Priority is set (not 'Undefined') and inheritance is documented.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: The impact-map.md states: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from TC-9003; no fixVersion scope setting found in Jira Field Defaults — defaulting to "both", so fixVersions will be propagated to tasks)'. The task-creation-log.md confirms: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 inherited from TC-9003 (Feature has non-empty fixVersions array; no fixVersion scope setting found in Jira Field Defaults, defaulting to "both" which propagates to tasks)' and shows each task receiving 'fixVersions: [RHTPA 1.5.0]' in additional_fields. The fixVersion scope is absent from CLAUDE.md, correctly defaulting to 'both', and inheritance is documented.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: The file summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains a '## Inherited Field Values' section stating: 'Priority: Critical (inherited from TC-9003, propagated to all tasks)' and 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from TC-9003, propagated to all tasks — fixVersion scope defaults to "both")'. The impact-map.md also has an '## Inherited Fields' section with the same information. Both documents clearly summarize the inherited field propagation.
